rounds.text: Studio LSD Ltd is priced at a deep and unwarranted discount to its intrinsic net worth, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.64x based on a share price of ₹ 9.80 against a book value of ₹ 15.3 [E1]. This valuation compression is even more stark when benchmarked externally, where the company's price-to-book ratio sits at an attractive 0.53x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.16x [E6]. Beneath the recent cyclical noise, the company demonstrates a proven ability to generate substantial shareholder returns over time, boasting a remarkable 5-year median return on equity of 28% alongside a robust 3-year median return on equity of 25% [E18, E19]. These stellar multi-year profitability metrics are formally recognized by the company's track record, which highlights a strong 3-year ROE of 25.2% [E37]. Conceded: the company currently faces a negative trailing P/E of -48.16x [E5], a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3], and a depressed recent ROE of -1.9% [E12] that places the stock near the bottom of its 52-week range [E4].

Studio LSD Ltd is currently burning capital, demonstrated by a deeply negative price-to-earnings ratio of -48.16x compared to a sector benchmark of 18.15x [E5]. This lack of profitability translates into negative returns for shareholders, with the company posting a trailing return on equity of -1.9% according to filed statements and -1.26% against a sector benchmark of 3.46% [E8, E12]. Market sentiment heavily reflects these fundamental deterioration risks, as the stock languishes at just 7 percent of the way up its 52-week range [E4]. Furthermore, the immediate operational trajectory shows deterioration, with the median return on equity over the last year dropping to -2% alongside a specific scanX signal engine screen reason highlighting this low ROE [E20, E44]. Investors also receive zero income protection or return of capital during this downturn, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: the company maintains a solid historical return on equity track record, boasting a 5-year median of 28%, a 3-year median of 25%, and a 3-year flagged ROE of 25.2% [E18, E19, E37].

Conceded: the company trades at a price-to-book ratio of 0.64x [E1] and 0.53x against a sector benchmark of 1.16x [E6], alongside historical median ROEs of 28% over five years and 25% over three years [E18, E19, E37]. However, framing this discount as "unwarranted" ignores the severe fundamental deterioration captured by the recent median ROE of -2% [E20], a trailing annual ROE of -1.9% [E12], and a screen flag for low ROE at -2% [E44]. The multi-year profitability track record cited by the bull is entirely decoupled from the current reality of a negative trailing P/E of -48.16x [E5] and an absolute zero dividend yield [E3]. This collapse into unprofitability explains why the stock sits languishing at a mere 7% of the way up its 52-week range [E4], invalidating the notion that historical returns justify buying distressed book value [E1].
